@crondaemon As a special case, should double entries (e.g. `-Tpdml -Tpdml`) be accepted? It would not cause the issue reported in #17139.
Is that a real case? Why would one issue double `-Tpdml`?

I was thinking about someone using a shellscript with some preset options or someone lazily building a line command line manually.

Usually the CLI parser is forgiving and allows you to configure unusual combinations. This special treatment of the `-T` option is an exception. I don't feel strongly about this though, but was flagging a potential edge case.

Either case, wouldn't it be bad to allow multiple options that pollute the expected output? I took a random software that has a strong command line support (nmap). What would you expect from this?

```
$ nmap -p 80 192.168.1.1 -p 55
```

To scan port 80, port 55 or both? Nmap has the answer for you

```
$ nmap -p 80 192.168.1.1 -p 55
Only 1 -p option allowed, separate multiple ranges with commas.
QUITTING!
```

and forces you to run the right one

```
$ nmap -p 80,55 192.168.1.1
```

that is ambiguous no more. I think the ambiguity should be fixed in -T as well. What do you think?

commits_data.message:
tshark: prevent multiple -T.

Subsequent use of -T option infere to each other
creating strange option combinations. Multiple -T
are not supported, then prevent them.

Fix: #17139.
